## Solution

**Setup.** Let $n = 2012$. The set $S$ is the $\ell^1$-ball (cross-polytope) $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \sum |x_i| \le 1\}$, whose $2n$ vertices are $\{\pm e_1, \dots, \pm e_n\}$. The set $T$ is the $\ell^\infty$-sphere of radius $2$, i.e. the boundary of the cube $[-2,2]^n$.

**Projection onto $S$.** For $p \notin S$, the Euclidean closest point in $S$ is the projection onto the $\ell^1$-ball, given by soft-thresholding:
$$x_i^* = \operatorname{sign}(p_i)\,(|p_i| - \lambda)_+, \qquad \text{where } \sum_{i=1}^n (|p_i|-\lambda)_+ = 1,\ \lambda \ge 0.$$
Since $p \in T$ has some $|p_j|=2$, we have $\|p\|_1 \ge 2 > 1$, so the constraint is active.

**When is the projection a vertex?** The projection $x^*$ equals a vertex $\pm e_j$ iff exactly one coordinate is nonzero, i.e. $|p_j| - \lambda = 1$ and $|p_i| \le \lambda$ for all $i \ne j$. This gives $\lambda = |p_j| - 1 \ge 0$ (so $|p_j| \ge 1$) and
$$|p_i| \le |p_j| - 1 \quad \text{for all } i \ne j. \tag{$\ast$}$$

Since $\max_i |p_i| = 2$, the coordinate $j$ in $(\ast)$ must satisfy $|p_j| = 2$ (if $|p_j| < 2$, some other coordinate equals $2 > |p_j|-1$, violating $(\ast)$). Thus the projection is a vertex iff there is a coordinate $j$ with $|p_j| = 2$ and $|p_i| \le 1$ for all $i \ne j$.

**Computing the probability.** The surface $T$ consists of $2n$ congruent faces, each an $(n{-}1)$-cube of side $4$, on which surface measure is uniform. By the symmetry of both $S$ and $T$ under coordinate permutations and sign changes, every face contributes equally. Consider the face $F = \{x_1 = 2,\ x_i \in [-2,2] \text{ for } i \ge 2\}$. On $F$, the vertex condition becomes $|x_i| \le 1$ for $i = 2, \dots, n$, i.e. each $x_i \in [-1,1]$.

Since each $x_i$ ($i \ge 2$) is uniform on $[-2,2]$ (length $4$) and must lie in $[-1,1]$ (length $2$), the probability on this face is
$$\left(\frac{2}{4}\right)^{n-1} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1}.$$

The same value holds on every face by symmetry, so the total probability is
$$\boxed{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2011}}.$$
